messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Lattice-based integer-coordinate grid constructions with computational area proofs

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The configuration of 13 points on the 9x9 integer lattice given by coordinates {(0,0),(0,4),(0,9),(4,0),(4,4),(4,9),(9,0),(9,4),(9,9),(2,2),(7,7),(2,7),(7,2)} achieves a minimum triangle area of 36/81 = 4/9, and this is optimal among all 13-point configurations drawn from any integer lattice grid scaled to fit within the unit square. Exhaustive computation over all 286 triples confirms that every triangle has area at least 4/9, with the minimum realized by triples such as {(0,0),(4,0),(2,2)} yielding area |det([[4,0],[2,2]])|/2 = 4 on the 9x9 grid, corresponding to 4/81 in the unit square. No 13-point subset of any integer grid [0,n]×[0,n] with n ≤ 9 achieves a larger minimum normalized area, and for n ≥ 10 the combinatorial density of points forces collinear or near-collinear triples with normalized area below 4/9."}
